source_reviews.independent_solution: With m=0.100 kg and nu=2 s^-1, omega=2*pi*nu=4*pi s^-1 and k=m*omega^2=1.6*pi^2 N/m, approximately 15.79 N/m. The fixed support, massless Hookean spring and negligible resistance justify the free simple-harmonic relation.

For the stated fixed-support, small-angle point-mass pendulum, T=2*pi*sqrt(l/g)=2*pi*sqrt((98 m)/g). At g=9.8 m/s^2, T=2*pi*sqrt(10) s, approximately 19.87 s. Retain the original historical setting and 98-meter datum without asserting a present-day apparatus measurement.
Equal elapsed time gives n1*T1=n2*T2, so T1/T2=6/10=3/5. At common g, l1/l2=(T1/T2)^2=9/25. Since l2-l1=16 cm, l1=9 cm and l2=25 cm; the faster first pendulum is shorter.

Surface gravity GM/r^2 gives gMoon/gEarth=(1/81)*(3.7)^2=13.69/81. Fixed-length small-angle T is proportional to 1/sqrt(g), so TMoon/TEarth=9/3.7, approximately 2.432. The period increases; gravity's ratio itself is not the period ratio.

Writing the string length as l, the suspended ball released from an extreme first reaches equilibrium after T/4=(pi/2)*sqrt(l/g). The ball dropped from the support traverses vertical distance l in tFall=sqrt(2*l/g). Since sqrt(2)<pi/2, the falling ball arrives first. Both start from rest simultaneously; this compares first arrivals, not total periods or path lengths alone.

Release from rest at 1 cm makes A=1 cm. In 2 s at 5 Hz there are 10 complete cycles. One cycle accumulates 4A of path length, giving s=40 cm=0.40 m. Net displacement after the integer number of cycles is zero, but is not the requested distance.

Differentiate x=5*cos(2*pi*t) cm: vx=-10*pi*sin(2*pi*t) cm/s. Speed amplitude is 10*pi cm/s. At the displacement phase 5*pi/6, sin(5*pi/6)=1/2, so signed vx=-5*pi cm/s. Displacement phase, not velocity phase, is supplied.

Use m=0.200 kg, k=16 N/m and A=0.020 m. omega=sqrt(k/m)=sqrt(80)=4*sqrt(5) rad/s. With the specified zero of potential energy, E=(1/2)*k*A^2=0.0032 J. vmax=omega*A=0.08*sqrt(5) m/s, approximately 0.1789 m/s. These are angular frequency, total mechanical energy and speed amplitude respectively.

The stipulated small block slides as a point mass with no rotation. Along the circular section, m*R*theta''=-m*g*sin(theta), hence theta''+(g/R)*theta=0 for small theta. Therefore T=2*pi*sqrt(R/g), independent of the mass; no rolling-inertia correction applies. Figure geometry is not freshly observed: supplied approved Chinese evidence reports center, radius R, small quadrilateral on the left slope, both bowl sides and full base, not a rolling body.

One main excitation per bump at spacing d=8 m makes forcing frequency f=v/d. The car's free frequency is f0=1/(1.5 s)=2/3 Hz. Weak-damping approximate resonance requires v/d approximately f0, yielding v=8/1.5 m/s=16/3 m/s, approximately 5.33 m/s or 19.2 km/h. Higher harmonics and nonlinear responses are expressly outside the source model.
